nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $F(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} f(k) - \sum_{k \ge 1} f(k + x)$, where a series that is not summable is given the value $0$. If the series $\sum_{k \ge 1} f(k)$ is summable, then $F(m) = f(1) + f(2) + \cdots + f(m)$ for every natural number $m$ (for $m = 0$ the right side is the empty sum $0$).
nodes.title: Ramanujan's extension agrees with the partial sums at natural numbers

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $F(y) = \sum_{k \ge 1} f(k) - \sum_{k \ge 1} f(k + y)$, where a series that is not summable is given the value $0$. If $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} f(k + x)$ is summable, then $F(x) - F(x - 1) = f(x)$.
nodes.title: Difference equation for Ramanujan's extension

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the extension of the partial sums of $f$ to real arguments is the function $F(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} f(k) - \sum_{k \ge 1} f(k + x)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, where each series is an unconditional sum and a series that is not summable is given the value $0$.
nodes.title: Ramanujan's extension of partial sums

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a natural number $q$, the constant $c_q$ is $\sum_{k \ge 1} f^{(q)}(k)$, the sum of the values of the $q$-th iterated derivative of $f$ at the positive integers, where a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$ and a series that is not summable is given the value $0$.
nodes.title: Ramanujan's derivative-series constants

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and a natural number $j$, the $j$-th term is $-c_{j+1} x^{j+1} / (j+1)!$, where $c_q = \sum_{k \ge 1} f^{(q)}(k)$ with $f^{(q)}$ the $q$-th iterated derivative of $f$; a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$ and a series that is not summable is given the value $0$.
nodes.title: Terms of the Taylor series in Entry 6

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a natural number $n$, the partial sum is $f(1) + f(2) + \cdots + f(n)$, which is $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Partial sums of a real function over the positive integers

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, natural numbers $q$ and $k$, and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the $k$-th term of the shifted series of $q$-th derivatives of $f$ is $f^{(q)}(k + 1 + x)$, where $f^{(q)}$ is the $q$-th iterated derivative of $f$ and a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Terms of the shifted derivative series

nodes.title: Taylor expansion of Ramanujan's extension at the origin

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $q$ be a natural number, and let $f^{(q)}$ be the $q$-th iterated derivative of $f$, where a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$. If the family $\bigl(f^{(q)}(k + 1)\bigr)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ is summable, then its sum is the constant $c_q = \sum_{k \ge 1} f^{(q)}(k)$.
nodes.title: The derivative-series constant is the sum of its series

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be infinitely differentiable and let $\rho > 0$. nodes.title: Derivatives of Ramanujan's extension at the origin

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be infinitely differentiable and let $\rho > 0$. Suppose that for every $q \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}$ the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} f^{(q)}(k + 1 + x)$ converges absolutely, and that for every $q \in \mathbb{N}$ there is a summable sequence $(b_k)_{k \ge 0}$ with $|f^{(q)}(k + 1 + x)| \le b_k$ for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $x \in [-\rho, \rho]$. nodes.title: Ramanujan's extension of the partial sums of a smooth function

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $q \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $f^{(q)}$ for the $q$-th iterated derivative of $f$, where a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$. If the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} f^{(q)}(k + 1)$ converges absolutely, then for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$ the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} f^{(q)}(k + 1 + m)$ converges absolutely.
nodes.title: Tails of the shifted series of derivatives converge

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
